commitResults.messageTitle: Level 0: rename Duke to Echo and greet the user
commitResults.messageBody:
- Rename Duke.java to Echo.java and update class name
  - Regenerate ASCII banner to spell 'Echo'
  - Update README.md and docs/README.md to use the new name
  - Print greeting and farewell wrapped by horizontal separator lines

- Read stdin line by line with Scanner
  - Print each line back inside a horizontal-line block
  - Exit the read loop when the user types exactly 'bye',
    then print the existing farewell block

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 2: store user input and list on demand
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add a fixed-size String[100] store with a running count (per spec)
  - Treat any non-command input as a new item and reply 'added: <item>'
  - On 'list', print stored items numbered 1..N inside the separator block
  - Keep 'bye' behavior unchanged

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 3: mark/unmark tasks and introduce Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
- Extract a Task class (description + isDone) per the A-Classes
    extension; override toString() so rendering lives in one place
  - Switch Echo's store from String[] to Task[]
  - Update 'list' output: add the 'Here are the tasks in your list:'
    header and the 'N.[X] desc' status-icon format
  - Add 'mark N' and 'unmark N' commands (1-based index) with the
    spec's confirmation messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 4: add Todo, Deadline, Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
- Introduce Todo, Deadline, Event subclasses of Task (A-Inheritance);
    each prepends its type tag ([T]/[D]/[E]) and appends type-specific
    suffix ((by: ...) / (from: ... to: ...))
  - Parse three new add commands: 'todo <desc>',
    'deadline <desc> /by <when>', 'event <desc> /from <when> /to <when>'
    (split with limit 2 to preserve slashes inside descriptions)
  - Replace the plain 'added: <item>' message with the spec's
    'Got it. I've added this task: ... Now you have N tasks in the list.'
    format, extracted into a small announceAdded() helper
  - Rely on polymorphism: Task[] still stores all subtypes; list, mark,
    and unmark branches are unchanged

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 5: handle bad input with a custom EchoException
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add EchoException (checked, extends Exception) per the A-Exceptions
    extension; catch it around the loop body and surface as 'OOPSgit add src/main/java/EchoException.java src/main/java/Echo.java! ...'
  - Restructure command dispatch to split-then-switch so bare commands
    ('todo', 'mark') are detected and routed to the right validator
  - Validate: empty descriptions for todo/deadline/event, missing /by
    /from /to, empty date fields, unknown commands, and (via new
    parseTaskIndex helper) missing / non-numeric / out-of-range task
    indices for mark and unmark
  - Fixes a latent crash: mark/unmark previously threw uncaught
    NumberFormatException or NullPointerException on bad indices

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 6: add 'delete' and migrate storage to ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody:
- Replace Task[100]+count with List<Task> backed by ArrayList
    (A-Collections extension); drops the 100-task assumption
  - Add 'delete N' command; reuses parseTaskIndex so it inherits the
    same missing/non-numeric/out-of-range validation as mark/unmark
  - Add symmetric announceRemoved() helper (mirrors announceAdded)
  - All other cases rewritten as one-to-one substitutions:
    items[i] -> items.get(i), items[count++]=t -> items.add(t),
    count -> items.size()

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: introduce TaskType enum for the [T]/[D]/[E] tags
commitResults.messageBody:
- New TaskType enum (TODO/DEADLINE/EVENT) carries the single-letter
    tag used in rendering; centralises what was three ad-hoc string
    literals scattered across the subclasses
  - Task now stores a TaskType and prints the tag itself, so Todo no
    longer needs a toString override, and Deadline/Event only add their
    own type-specific suffix
  - Purely a refactor: user-visible output is byte-identical

Echo currently loses all tasks when the program exits, since the
task list only lives in memory. The course's Level 7 requirement
is to persist tasks automatically and reload them on startup.

- Add Storage, which reads/writes the task list to data/echo.txt,
  creating the file and folder on first run if missing.
- Add Task#toFileFormat() (overridden in Deadline/Event) to
  serialize each task to a pipe-delimited line.
- Wire Storage into Echo: load tasks at startup, save after every
  mutating command (mark/unmark/delete/todo/deadline/event).
- Skip corrupted save-file lines with a warning instead of
  crashing, and ignore data/ in .gitignore since it holds a
  local runtime file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 7: fix Java convention issues in Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.java did not follow the intermediate Java convention
(se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html):
the constructor had no Javadoc, and parseLine's switch declared
`task` before assigning it inside each case instead of at
declaration.

- Add a Javadoc comment on the Storage constructor.
- Rewrite parseLine's switch as a switch expression so `task`
  is initialized where declared.
- Reindent the switch so `case` is one level deeper than
  `switch`, per the convention.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 7: fix Java convention issues in Echo
commitResults.messageBody:
Echo.java's dispatch switch did not follow the intermediate Java
convention (se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/
intermediate.html): `case` was indented at the same level as
`switch` instead of one level deeper, and two error messages
exceeded the 120-char line length limit.

- Reindent the switch so `case` is one level deeper than
  `switch`, and case-body statements one level deeper still.
- Wrap the deadline and event error messages that exceeded
  120 chars.

Echo previously stored deadline/event dates as opaque Strings, so
it could not validate, format, or query them. The course's Level 8
requirement is to parse dates as LocalDate and display them in a
friendlier format.

- Store Deadline.by and Event.from/to as LocalDate instead of
  String; accept yyyy-mm-dd input and print as "MMM dd yyyy" via
  a shared Task.DISPLAY_DATE_FORMAT constant.
- Reject unparsable dates and (for events) a '/to' before '/from'
  with a friendly EchoException instead of storing bad data.
- Add Task#occursOn(LocalDate), overridden per subclass, and a new
  'on <date>' command that lists tasks occurring on a given date
  (the level's stretch goal).
- Update Storage#parseLine to parse LocalDate from the save file;
  pre-Level-8 free-text dates are skipped as corrupted lines via
  the existing warning path, not crashed on.
- Remove an unused ArrayList import left over from Level 7.

The course's Level 7/A-MoreOOP AI-Guidance prompts suggest running
/test-ui and /present-changes-visually after each change, but
neither existed as a skill in this project or globally. Add both
as project-level skills so the upcoming Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList
refactor (A-MoreOOP) can follow that workflow:

- test-ui: compiles fresh and runs a scripted stdin regression
  script covering every current command, plus a second run to
  check save/load persistence, since this project has no JUnit
  test suite yet.
- present-changes-visually: publishes the current git diff as a
  colored HTML Artifact with a short rationale, instead of pasting
  a raw diff into the chat.

Echo's main() mixed three concerns in one method: console I/O
(banner, prompts, task confirmations, errors), command parsing, and
the command dispatch loop itself. The A-MoreOOP increment asks for
closely related code to be pulled out into classes, done gradually
in small steps. Ui (all interaction with the user) is the smallest,
lowest-risk first slice: every System.out/Scanner call moves out
verbatim, with no change to parsing or task-list logic.

- Add Ui: owns the Scanner and every printed message (welcome,
  goodbye, the divider line, list, add/remove/mark/unmark
  confirmations, date-filtered listing, error messages).
- Echo.main() now calls ui.readCommand()/ui.show*() instead of
  System.out.println/Scanner directly; parsing, task-list
  mutation, and Storage calls are unchanged.
- Ran the test-ui regression script before and after: transcript
  output is byte-for-byte identical, confirming this is a pure
  structural change with no behavior difference.

With Ui already extracted, Echo.main() still reaches into a raw
List<Task> directly for every add/remove/get/size call. The next
smallest slice per the A-MoreOOP target is TaskList: a class that
owns that list and the membership operations performed on it.

- Add TaskList: wraps a List<Task>, exposes add/remove/get/size
  and getAll() (for Ui rendering and Storage saving). Marking a
  task done/not-done stays Task's own responsibility
  (markAsDone/markAsNotDone) rather than moving here, since that's
  a property of one task, not list membership.
- Echo now holds a TaskList instead of a raw List<Task>; every
  items.* call becomes the equivalent tasks.* call, and
  storage.save(items) becomes storage.save(tasks.getAll()).
- Ran the test-ui regression script before and after: transcript
  output is byte-for-byte identical.

Echo.main()'s switch cases still mixed dispatch with the actual
work of interpreting each command's arguments (splitting on /by,
/from, /to, parsing dates, validating and throwing EchoException).
Parser takes over "making sense of the command," per the A-MoreOOP
target, leaving Echo's switch as pure dispatch: parse, then act.

- Add Parser: getCommandWord/getArguments replace the inline
  input.split(" ", 2); parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent build
  and validate each Task type; parseOnDate and parseTaskIndex
  moved verbatim from Echo. Every error message is unchanged.
- Echo's switch cases shrink to one Parser call plus the
  tasks/ui/storage calls that were already there; parseDate and
  parseTaskIndex are removed from Echo now that Parser owns them.
- Ran the test-ui regression script, plus a targeted check of the
  event to-before-from and bad-index error paths (both moved
  logic, not touched by earlier iterations): transcript output is
  byte-for-byte identical to before this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-MoreOOP: reshape Echo into an instance orchestrator
commitResults.messageBody:
With Ui, Storage, TaskList, and Parser all extracted, Echo was
still a static-only, main()-only class threading ui/storage/tasks
through local variables. This final increment reshapes it to match
the target design: instance fields wired up in a constructor, a
run() loop, and a thin static main().

- Add fields ui/storage/tasks and a Echo(String filePath)
  constructor that wires them up (mirrors the target's example
  Duke(String filePath) constructor).
- Move the read-then-decide loop into run(); it's unchanged except
  that cmd/rest dispatch now reads the instance fields instead of
  locals.
- main() is now new Echo("data/echo.txt").run() — Echo no longer
  does any work itself, only orchestrates Ui/Storage/TaskList/
  Parser, which is the shape the A-MoreOOP target asks for.
- Storage.load() already swallows IO/parse errors internally and
  returns an empty list with a warning (from Level 7's design),
  so the constructor doesn't need the target example's
  try/catch(DukeException) — that concern is already handled one
  layer down, in Storage itself.
- Ran the test-ui regression script (full command coverage plus
  the persistence round-trip run): transcript output is
  byte-for-byte identical to before this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Packages: organize classes into echo.* packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All 11 classes lived flat under src/main/java with no package
declaration. This increment splits them into packages by
responsibility, going straight for the stretch goal (multiple
packages) rather than the minimal single-package bar, since the
boundaries already exist from the A-MoreOOP refactor.

- echo (root): Echo, EchoException — entry point and the one
  exception type used across the app; too small/central to split
  further, and EchoException would be a single-file package on
  its own.
- echo.task: Task, TaskType, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList —
  the whole task domain model and its collection wrapper, the
  most cohesive group in the codebase.
- echo.ui, echo.storage, echo.parser: one package each, mapping
  directly onto the Ui/Storage/Parser classes A-MoreOOP already
  extracted. Named echo.parser rather than mirroring the example's
  echo.command, since there's no Command-pattern here — the
  package name should describe what the design actually has.
- src/main/java stays the source root per the course's explicit
  warning; src/main/java themselves are not packages.
- Files moved with git mv to preserve history; each gained a
  package declaration and the cross-package imports it needed
  (java.* imports first, echo.* imports after, per the project's
  Java convention).
- Updated the test-ui skill: the compile step now needs a
  recursive `find` instead of a flat src/main/java/*.java glob,
  and the entry point is echo.Echo, not Echo.
- Ran the test-ui regression script against the new echo.Echo
  entry point: transcript output is byte-for-byte identical to
  before this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix stale Gradle template mainClass and jar name
commitResults.messageBody:
The add-gradle-support merge brought in the generic Duke
template's build.gradle, which still pointed at seedu.duke.Duke
and duke.jar. This project's entry point is echo.Echo (from
A-Packages), so `./gradlew run` would have failed with a
class-not-found error.

- application.mainClass: seedu.duke.Duke -> echo.Echo
- shadowJar.archiveFileName: duke.jar -> echo.jar

Verified `./gradlew run` works correctly with the fix.

Adds JUnit 5 tests for the Minimal requirement: at least two
non-trivial methods across two different classes, tested well
enough to catch most potential bugs in the target methods.

- TodoTest (echo.task): toString() in both done/not-done states,
  toFileFormat()'s save-line format, occursOn() always false
  (Todo has no date).
- ParserTest (echo.parser): parseDeadline() and parseEvent(), the
  two most branch-heavy methods in the codebase. Covers the happy
  path plus every distinct failure mode each method can hit
  (missing clauses, empty fields, unparsable dates, and the
  '/to' before '/from' check for events) rather than just the
  successful case.
- Both test classes mirror their target class's package under
  src/test/java, per Gradle's test-discovery convention.

Ran `./gradlew test`: all 13 tests pass. Stopping at the Minimal
bar here rather than the Stretch goal (testing every class).

commitResults.messageTitle: A-JavaDoc: document all non-private classes and methods
commitResults.messageBody:
An audit found classes were well covered (10/11 had header
comments) but methods were not (only 10/50, ~20%) -- combined
coverage was ~33%, short of the 50% Minimal bar either way "half"
is read (combined pool, or classes and methods counted
separately). Rather than add just enough to clear 50%, this goes
for the Stretch goal, since the codebase is small (61 items total)
and AGENTS.md already asks for Javadoc on "all classes and...
nontrivial methods" as a standing convention.

- Added header comments to every non-private class (Echo was the
  one gap) and every non-private method across all 11 files,
  including constructors and simple getters.
- Added comments to the two non-trivial private helpers that
  lacked them: Parser#parseDate and Storage#ensureFileExists.
  (Storage#parseLine already had one.)
- Followed the project's existing dual style: trivial one-liners
  get a compact single-line /** ... */; methods with real
  parameters/exceptions (mainly Parser's command parsers, and
  constructors) get full @param/@throws blocks, matching the
  precedent already set by Storage's constructor.
- Verified with `javac -Xdoclint:all`: zero errors, compiles
  clean. Re-tallied coverage: 11/11 classes, 50/50 non-private
  methods documented.
- Ran the test-ui regression script and `./gradlew test`: output
  and all 13 JUnit tests are unchanged -- this is a comments-only
  change, no behavior difference.

Captures the SE-EDU intermediate Java convention
(se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html) as a
project skill covering naming, layout/indentation, line length,
brackets, statement form, and Javadoc format, so it can be
consulted (and enforced) whenever Java code in this repo is
written or edited, not just during one-off review passes.

- Add .claude/skills/seedu-java-coding-standard/SKILL.md.
- Update AGENTS.md to mandate following it for all Java code in
  this project, pointing at the skill for the actual rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CodingStandard: fix convention violations in existing code
commitResults.messageBody:
Audited the codebase against the newly-added
seedu-java-coding-standard skill and fixed what it flagged:

- TodoTest/ParserTest: import order was wrong -- a plain
  (non-static) org.junit.jupiter.api.Test import came before the
  static Assertions imports. Convention orders static imports
  first, then java.*, then third-party groups.
- Storage#parseLine: one switch-expression line (119 chars) was
  under the 120 hard limit but over the 110 soft limit; wrapped it
  the same way the rest of the file already wraps long lines.
- TaskType#tag(): renamed to getTag(). Convention requires method
  names to be verbs; "tag" is a noun. Left TaskList#size() as-is,
  since it mirrors java.util.Collection#size() -- an established
  Java API name, not a project-specific noun needing a fix.

Ran the test-ui regression script and `./gradlew test`: output
and all 13 JUnit tests are unchanged -- this is a style-only pass,
no behavior difference.

Same motivation as seedu-java-coding-standard: capture the SE-EDU
git convention (se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html) as
a project skill so it's applied to every commit message and
branch name going forward, not just checked occasionally.

- Add .claude/skills/seedu-git-standard/SKILL.md, covering
  subject-line length/mood/capitalization, body wrapping and
  structure, and kebab-case branch naming.
- Update AGENTS.md's Git section to mandate it for all future
  commits and branches, pointing at the skill for the rules.
  Past commits are not being rewritten -- only new ones follow
  this from here on.

Users had no way to locate a task without scrolling through the
whole list. This adds `find <keyword>`, listing every task whose
description contains the keyword (case-insensitive).

- Task#matchesKeyword(String): case-insensitive substring check
  against the description. Lives on the base Task class rather
  than being overridden per subclass (unlike occursOn), since
  matching is purely about the description, which every task type
  shares unchanged.
- Parser#parseFindKeyword(String): validates a keyword was given,
  same shape as the other single-argument parse methods.
- Ui#showMatchingTasks(List<Task>): prints numbered matches with
  a "(none)" fallback, mirroring showTasksOnDate's style for the
  other filtered-view command.
- Echo's new "find" case filters tasks.getAll() into a match list
  the same way the "on" case already does, for consistency between
  the two query-style commands.
- Added TaskTest (matchesKeyword: match, case-insensitive match,
  no match) and two ParserTest cases (valid keyword, empty
  keyword). Ran the test-ui regression script (existing commands
  unchanged; find's example from the spec reproduces exactly) and
  `./gradlew test`: all 16 tests pass.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/echo/task/TaskType.java

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/echo/parser/Parser.java

parseDeadline and parseEvent named their split() results p, p1,
and p2, which don't say what they hold and are easy to mix up.

A PR reviewer flagged this as unclear. Rename them to parts,
fromParts, and toParts so each name reflects which clause it was
split on, matching the plural-array naming already used in
getArguments().

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command dispatch out of the run() loop
commitResults.messageBody:
run() mixed two concerns: the read-command loop, and the switch
that executes one command. That made the switch hard to reuse
from anywhere other than this loop.

Move the switch into a new executeCommand(cmd, rest) method so a
future caller (e.g. a GUI controller, planned for a later
increment) can dispatch a single command the same way the console
loop does, instead of duplicating or re-deriving this logic.

Behaviour is unchanged; verified by comparing CLI output before
and after the extraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CheckStyle: add Checkstyle Gradle plugin and config
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the 'checkstyle' Gradle plugin and config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml
and suppressions.xml, copied from AddressBook Level 3
(https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/config/checkstyle),
which already encodes the SE-EDU intermediate Java coding standard this
project follows. Run via `gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest`.

Test classes are suppressed from the JavadocType and
MissingJavadocMethodCheck rules, matching this project's existing
convention (seedu-java-coding-standard skill) that test classes/methods
may skip header Javadoc.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CheckStyle: fix violations found by Checkstyle
commitResults.messageBody:
Running checkstyleTest flagged 3 SeparatorWrap violations in
ParserTest.java: a lambda's empty parameter list "()" started a
wrapped continuation line instead of staying on the previous line.

Move the wrap point to after "->" instead, so the lambda's "()"
stays attached to assertThrows(...) on the first line. checkstyleMain
was already clean.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 10: add JavaFX dependency and Echo.getResponse()
commitResults.messageBody:
A GUI needs a way to get Echo's reply to one command as a String,
instead of driving the console read-loop that run() uses.

Add getResponse(String), which executes one command through the
existing executeCommand() dispatch and returns what Ui would have
printed, by temporarily redirecting System.out into a buffer for
the call. This reuses run()'s logic as-is rather than duplicating
it, since executeCommand() was already extracted for this purpose
in a previous increment.

Also add the JavaFX dependencies to build.gradle, copied from the
JavaFX Tutorial's sample build.gradle rather than improvised, since
the per-OS classifiers there are what keep the build portable across
Windows/macOS/Linux. Point application.mainClass at the new GUI
entry point (added in the next commit) so `gradlew run` opens the
GUI by default; the plain CLI (echo.Echo) is still runnable directly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 10: add JavaFX GUI (MainWindow, DialogBox, Launcher)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a GUI on top of the existing console UI, following the JavaFX
Tutorial (Parts 1-5): Launcher works around the classpath issue of
the Application subclass also being the entry point; Main loads
MainWindow.fxml and injects a shared Echo instance; MainWindow turns
each Enter/Send into one Echo#getResponse() call and renders the
exchange as a pair of DialogBox bubbles; DialogBox colour-codes
Echo's reply by command word (add/mark/unmark/delete) the same way
the tutorial's dialog boxes are styled by command type.

FXML, CSS, and avatar/background assets are adapted from the
completed javafx-tutorial project, with two changes: classes moved
into the echo.gui package (a class needs a package under this
project's coding standard), and the user avatar path corrected to
DaUser.jpeg (the tutorial project's own DialogBox.java references
DaUser.png, but the actual asset file is a .jpeg).

Typing "bye" still closes the app, same as the console UI: it shows
the farewell message, then exits after a short pause so the message
is visible. The console UI (echo.Echo) is unchanged and still fully
usable on its own.

Verified: gradlew compileJava/checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest/test all
pass; the GUI was launched and visually confirmed to render (title,
avatar, background, initial greeting, input field); Echo#getResponse
was smoke-tested directly for todo/list/mark/delete/blank/unknown/bye
inputs, matching the console UI's behaviour for the same commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Varargs: use varargs for Ui's multi-line messages
commitResults.messageBody:
showTaskAdded/Removed/Marked/Unmarked each printed 2-3 fixed lines
via repeated System.out.println calls, with no shared helper.

Add a private printLines(String...) and have those four methods
call it instead. Varargs fits well here specifically because every
call site already knows its exact line count at compile time and
passes literals, rather than assembling a List<String> first, which
is exactly the "small, known-in-advance argument list" case varargs
is for.

Behaviour is unchanged; verified by comparing CLI output for
todo/mark/unmark/delete before and after.
